title: Against Rounded Personality - The Lonely Crowd by David Riesman
original:
David Riesman’s The Lonely Crowd 한국어판 p.148-p.157 제 3장 “동료에 의한 심판" 중 “선호의 사회화"에서 발췌

  “때로는 상품의 소비뿐 아니라 정서생활에 관한 취향까지도 철저히 사회화된다. 그 결과 아이들은 남과 의미 없는 잡담하는 법을 배우게 된다.” 
  “... 자신이 동료들과 동떨어진 유별난 존재가 돼버릴지 모륻나는 그들의 공포심은 참으로 엄청났다…”
  “... 나는 우리 아이가 모든 면에서 평범한 아이가 되기를 바랍니다.”
  “좋은 집이나 멋진 말, 아름다운 여자, 또는 값진 예술품에 대한 욕망이란 소비자 기호에 따른 가치의 상실이나 변화가 생기는 순수 소비라기보다는 일종의 투자와 다름없기 때문이다.”
  “아이들의 만화와 장난감을 소비하는 데 반해 어른들은 신문 사설이나 자동차를 소비한다. 그러나 그 둘은 갈수록 비슷한 방식으로 소비생활을 즐기게 된다.”
  
  Rounded Personality → Appears in a Job description, recruitment, student admission process (입학사정관제).... The value considered when recruiting a new person - or, a new slave. A new person can be substituted from person A to person B. Person A and Person B → Identitial if they are ‘rounded’. Average, just normal. Normal person, normal people…
  
  We are trained to be ‘rounded’, to be socialised → i.e., within David Riesman’s perspective, to share the contemporary trend with peers and adjust ourselves to cultural preferences within it. Thus, we consume the same, we listen to the same, we think the same… And that’s how you become a ‘rounded’ person. The same kind of manufactured person, with slightly different expertise, but that’s all - The rest of the preferences are identitcal from one to another. 
  
  Nietzschestic vision of ubermensch is dead within this perspective… Ubermensch is not a rounded person, it might lack in some aspects, but very strong in other aspects…. Ubermensch is never rounded, innovation does not come from a rounded personality (It is only the branded innovation that a rounded personality can make). Definitely, the strong and resilient humanity’s future will be based on how we get out of this treadmill of consumerism-Regresstion_to_the_mean (in terms of personality, education, preferences, etc.) Destroy the landscape of existing preference towards rounded personality, destroy the existing frameworks, if we don’t want the history of humanity to terminate by the rise of machines.
english:
Reading David Riesman’s The Lonely Crowd, particularly the discussion of socialised preferences in the Korean edition, pages 148–157, I was struck by how extensively peer judgement can organise both consumption and emotional life. The passages I copied concern fear of standing apart, the wish for an ordinary child, possessions as investments in social value, and the increasingly similar ways children and adults consume. These are my notes on those passages, not a quotation from an English edition.

The ‘well-rounded personality’ appears everywhere: job descriptions, recruitment criteria, university admissions. It sounds generous, but I hear another possibility in it—the wish for a person who is readily substitutable. If person A and person B are both acceptably rounded, the institution can exchange one for the other.

We are trained to become rounded by being socialised: following our peers’ trends, learning the same preferences, consuming the same things. We acquire different specialisms while the rest of our lives converge. The result resembles a manufactured personality with a few adjustable features.

This is difficult to reconcile with my reading of Nietzsche’s Übermensch. Such a figure need not be balanced in every respect. They may be weak in one area and forceful in another. A new value does not necessarily emerge from the person most comfortably fitted to existing expectations. What passes as innovation within that fit may be little more than branded innovation.

I want to resist this treadmill of consumption and regression towards the mean—in personality, education and preference. If we train people chiefly to meet an existing template, we also train them to resemble the machines that may perform that template more efficiently. The task is to challenge the preference for roundedness itself.
